title: Expansion of tumor-infiltrating and marrow-infiltrating lymphocytes from pediatric malignant solid tumors
markdown:
## Protocol: I have fresh pediatric solid-tumor samples and bone-marrow samples and need to establish the first cultures of tumor-infiltrating and marrow-infiltrating lymphocytes. Describe how to process the two sample types separately, maintain and expand the initial cultures, and collect cells for viability and basic phenotype checks. Limit this workflow to the primary-culture stage.

### Overview

This protocol outlines the primary culture workflow for establishing tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL) from fresh pediatric solid-tumor samples and marrow-infiltrating lymphocytes (MIL) from bone-marrow specimens. The process involves separate acquisition and processing of tissue and marrow, initial seeding in IL-2-supplemented media, maintenance through weekly media changes and splitting upon confluence, and final collection at week 4 for viability assessment and basic phenotypic analysis via flow cytometry.

### Materials/Reagents

RPMI media; Interleukin-2 (IL-2); Cell Preparation Tubes (CPT tubes, BD Biosciences); Heparinized phosphate buffered solution; Ficoll density gradient reagent; Red blood cell lysis buffer; Trypan blue; Zombie NIR stain; Antibodies against CD3, CD4, CD8, and CD56.

### Equipment

24-well tissue culture plates; BD Celesta flow cytometer; FACSDiva software; FlowJo software; Standard sterile tissue processing equipment (mincing tools, centrifuges).

### Safety & Sterility

All procedures must be performed under sterile conditions. Specimens must be deidentified and labeled with a unique study ID prior to processing.

## Sample Acquisition and Processing

### Day 0: Sample Acquisition

1. Immediately following tissue acquisition under sterile conditions, allocate a fresh tumor sample (>1 cm³) in RPMI media by the pathologist, confirming sufficient tissue availability for clinical care. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Obtain bone marrow specimens via aspiration as part of standard-of-care or via reamings from the marrow cavity prior to endoprosthetic reconstruction in resected bone tumors. Collect 10–20 mL of bone marrow in either a CPT tube (BD Biosciences) for aspirates or in heparinized phosphate buffered solution for orthopedic surgeries. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Deidentify all specimens and label them with a unique study ID. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->
4. Process a portion or all of the specimen for TIL culture; use the remaining specimen for tumor digest in reactivity assays when feasible. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S04 -->
5. Review Hematoxylin and eosin-stained (H&E) slides representative of allocated tumor samples with the lowest and highest TIL growth by an institutional pathologist to determine tumor content and evaluate the pattern of immune cell infiltration. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S05 -->
6. Prepare tumors by mincing fragments into pieces approximately 1 mm³ in size and explanting them into at least 12 wells (1 fragment per well) of a 24-well plate containing culture media supplemented with interleukin-2 (IL-2) at 6000 IU/mL. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S06 -->
7. Process bone marrow specimens using Ficoll density gradient centrifugation, then treat the resulting white blood cells with red blood cell lysis buffer to remove red blood cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S07 -->

### Primary Expansion Phase (PreREP)

1. Assess cell viability using trypan blue exclusion. Resuspend cells in culture media supplemented with IL-2 (6000 IU/mL) at a concentration of 5 × 10⁶ live cells/mL. Seed 1 × 10⁶ live cells in a final volume of 2 mL into a single well of a 24-well tissue culture plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S01 -->
2. Score MIL proliferation every 3 days. Remove one-half of the culture media from the top without disturbing the cells and replenish with fresh media containing 6000 IU/mL IL-2 every 3 days to maintain MIL proliferation for 4 weeks. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S02 -->
3. When wells reach 80% cell confluency, split MILs 1:2 into new wells and replenish with fresh culture media supplemented with IL-2 (6000 IU/mL). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S03 -->
4. Remove one-half of the media containing IL-2 and replenish with fresh culture media supplemented with IL-2 (6000 IU/mL) every 3 days to maintain TIL proliferation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S04 -->
5. When TIL reaches 80% confluency within the well, split TIL 1:2 into a new well of a 24-well plate and replenish with fresh media containing 6000 IU/mL IL-2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S05 -->

### Week 4: Final Collection

1. After 4 weeks of initial culture, collect the final TIL product, count the cells, and prepare for phenotypic and reactivity assays. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T2-S01 -->

### Phenotypic Analysis

1. To determine the phenotype of TIL/MIL, stain approximately 2.5 × 10⁵ cells with Zombie NIR and surface markers CD3, CD4, CD8, and CD56. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T3-S01 -->
2. Perform single-cell acquisition using a BD Celesta flow cytometer and FACSDiva software. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T3-S02 -->
3. Analyze data using FlowJo software. Report the phenotype of the TIL/MIL product as a percentage of the live cell population. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T3-S03 -->

## References

- [1] Expansion of tumor-infiltrating and marrow-infiltrating lymphocytes from pediatric malignant solid tumors — https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcyt.2024.08.002
